As carried by search-result summaries of the abstract (not verbatim-verified): constraints on the electron's Lorentz-symmetry-breaking coefficients (SME c_MN / c_JK, Sun-centred frame) improved 'to the 10^-21 level' by composite-pulse Ramsey spectroscopy in the Yb+ 2F7/2 manifold. (READ)'; branelink.py:97-98 '|c| <= 6.37e-64 against a 1e-21 laboratory bound -- 42 orders short, a real measurement that does not bite'; branelink.py:308 SME_ORDERS_SHORT = log10(SME_LAB_BOUND / sme_coefficient()).
published_hypotheses: (from search summaries, not READ) The bound is on the ELECTRON sector's c coefficients -- not photon, proton or any other species.

(from search summaries, not READ) It bounds the spatial, anisotropic components (c_{X-Y} = c_XX - c_YY, c_XY, c_XZ, c_YZ; possibly c_ZZ-type combination) in the Sun-centred celestial-equatorial frame, via the sidereal modulation of an orbital-quadrupole energy shift of a Michelson-Morley-type test; it does NOT bound c_TT or isotropic parts at 1e-21.

(standard for this class of measurement; not READ here) The conversion from a measured frequency modulation to c_JK uses an atomic-structure matrix element for the Yb+ 2F7/2 state from theory, and takes all other SME coefficients as zero (one-coefficient-at-a-time / electron-only analysis).
(not READ) The '10^-21 level' is per-component with stated uncertainties (1 sigma or a stated CL); the exact per-component values and CL were not seen.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the authors had (per summaries): a single Yb+ ion, composite-pulse Ramsey in 2F7/2 with > 1 s coherence, a sidereal-modulation fit in the Sun-centred frame, and a theoretical atomic matrix element to convert frequency to c_JK. What came later: no superseding electron c_JK measurement was found; atomic-structure recalculations of the Yb+ 2F7/2 quadrupole matrix element could shift the bound by an O(1)-to-O(10) factor at most -- not checked here. Does missing data change the conclusion the TREE draws? No, computed: the tree's conclusion ('42 orders short at r = 38.6 um, beta = 1') would survive any revision of the bound by up to ~40 orders in either direction (rederive (b)). The data the tree itself lacks matters more than any the authors lacked: (1) the lab's velocity B relative to the compactification frame, needed to project KN's c_{mu nu} onto the components Dreissen actually bounds -- UNMEASURED, and on a hypothetical structure its absence makes the tree's comparison conservative; (2) r, which the tree fixes at its largest allowed value, the least-biting point. Evidence either way: no datum the authors lacked is shown to move anything here.
grade_evidence: The source could not be READ in this stage (alphaXiv quota refused on every call; every publisher/repository host refused by the egress proxy), so the value 1e-21 -- marked 'READ' at branelink.py:149 -- is not re-verified against the paper's table, and its hypotheses (electron sector; spatial anisotropic c_JK in the Sun-centred frame; other coefficients zero; CL) are known here only from search-result summaries. By the docket's rule a claim that cannot be checked here is OPEN, and it is not flattened to STANDS. What WAS computed: the tree's arithmetic stands exactly (|c| = 6.372e-64, 42.196 orders -> 42), and the dependent conclusion O7's SME null is insensitive to the bound's value by ~40 orders, so no plausible correction to the datum moves it. Two scope notes, both recorded not repaired: (i) a probable dropped hypothesis -- the bound constrains Sun-frame c_JK components, not a scalar |c|, and the projection needs the unmeasured B; on a hypothetical structure that drop is conservative (runs against biting); (ii) LEDGER.md:101 / ledger.py:1793 restate the null without branelink.py:96-97's '(r = 38.6 um, beta = 1)'; the same bound does bite at beta = 1 for r <= 3.08e-26 m. Neither is shown to be an error in Dreissen et al., and nothing here is WRONG.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading arXiv:2206.00570 (Table of fitted c_JK with uncertainties and CL, the atomic matrix element used, the frame and sector) and Kabat & Nomura arXiv:2309.05759 eqs. 76-77 (tensor structure of c_{mu nu}, definition of mu, and the sentence quoting the ~1e-21 bound). If every bounded component is at <= a few x 1e-21, electron sector, Sun-centred frame -> STANDS for the value, with the tree's comparison graded NARROWED on the component/frame hypothesis unless KN's c maps onto c_JK with O(1) weight independent of B. If KN's c is purely c_TT-type in the compactification frame, Dreissen's bound applies only through B^2 and the comparison is NARROWED (conservatively). If the table shows the relevant components are bounded only at 1e-19 or weaker, the value is a discrepancy (DATA-DEPENDENT in principle) but rederive (b) already shows the 42-orders conclusion moves by at most 2 orders.
